critic_notes.rationale: This is a direct rank-product of two of the most heavily published anomalies (book-to-market and Sloan total accruals) with no genuine conditioning structure — since both legs are independently positive predictors, the product behaves like a naive composite score rather than an interaction, and value-plus-accrual-quality screens are already standard (Piotroski, Desai-Rajgopal-Venkatachalam).

Scaling cash flow by earnings (oancf/ib) is numerically unstable and non-monotone around ib≈0 and sign-flipping for loss firms, so the "cash conversion" leg does not measure what the hypothesis claims, and the underlying idea is essentially the published cash-based-profitability/accruals refinement of earnings yield.

Compustat recch and invch are cash-flow-statement items stated as sources/(uses) of cash, so a receivables/inventory buildup enters as a *negative* number and the NEG() wrapper inverts the intended penalty — the expression likely rewards exactly the accrual-heavy "value traps" the hypothesis wants to avoid.

The most substantively constructed proposal of the batch (balance-sheet working-capital accruals interacted with an EBITDA/EV multiple rather than a generic B/M-plus-accruals stack), though it remains close to known EV-multiple and accrual anomalies and needs handling of negative enterprise values, which perversely map cash-rich cheap firms into the lowest rank.

Near-duplicate of "Clean Book Value Cross" with a hard 0/1 gate that piles roughly half the universe at exactly zero, so the short leg becomes an arbitrary mixture of low-B/M and gated-out high-B/M firms and the resulting spread is not interpretable as the stated conditional value effect.

The expected sign contradicts the expression's natural direction — the composite assigns its highest values to high earnings-yield firms, whose dominant unconditional effect is positive, so a "value trap" test requires conditioning or differencing within the value leg rather than a rank product; the 3-period TREND on an annual accrual ratio is also very noisy.

The expression correctly implements Sloan's balance-sheet accrual and subtracts it from earnings, but ib minus accruals is definitionally cash flow, so the signal is simply cash-flow-to-price — a long-published value measure (LSV 1994) rather than a genuine accrual–value interaction.

wcap = act − lct includes cash and short-term debt, so DELTA(wcap,1) penalizes firms that simply accumulate cash or repay current debt — the opposite of the stated "profits absorbed by receivable/inventory investment" mechanism, making the construct inconsistent with the hypothesis.

The recch sign convention is handled correctly, but this is the EBITDA-base analogue of the already-tested and failed "Working Capital Realized Sales Yield," with a tiny cash-flow-statement adjustment that will be swamped by the known EBITDA-yield component and the same sparse recch coverage.

Sign conventions and hypothesis are internally consistent and the supplier-financing-quality mechanism is a distinct, economically defensible refinement of cash-flow yield, though the dominant oancf/price component means the incremental content over a known anomaly may be modest.

critic_notes.target_name: Cumulative Working Capital Clean Book Yield
critic_notes.rationale: TS_SUM of first differences telescopes to a simple three-year change in wcap, so the "cumulative accrual accumulation" framing is illusory, and wcap's inclusion of cash and current debt again inverts the intended economics while subtracting a flow-change from book equity is dimensionally incoherent.

The two sales-yield terms cancel exactly, so the expression reduces to industry-adjusted −(recch+invch)/market cap — a price-scaled working-capital accrual measure with no value interaction at all, contradicting the stated "cheap-but-accrual-dependent value trap" hypothesis.

The EV floor at market equity is a substantive fix to the negative-enterprise-value misranking that plausibly explains the archived EBITDA-yield signals' broken portfolio alphas, but the numerator is a recombination of two already-tested weak constructs and inherits their ~7-11% coverage, so upside is limited.

This is the archived "One Sided Accrual Capped Earnings Yield" wrapped in a standard industry demean — a cosmetic transformation of an existing archive entry, and intra-industry value (Asness-Porter-Stevens) is itself a published anomaly rather than a new mechanism.

Economically this is the Sloan operating-accrual anomaly restricted to high E/P firms (a well-documented value-accrual interaction), and mechanically the double indicator sets the signal to exactly zero for the large majority of firms, so the "long" leg is a mass of ties and portfolio composition will be unstable.

Same degenerate construction as the prior proposal (most firms pinned at exactly zero) compounded by apalch's already-thin ~6% coverage, and the underlying payables-stretch mechanism has already failed twice in the archive without diagnosis of why.

Delta taxes payable is tiny relative to income for almost all firms, so ib - max(0, Δtxp) over market equity will be near-perfectly correlated with plain earnings yield — this is effectively a rediscovery of E/P with a negligible perturbation.

Penalizing the valuation denominator by scaled accrual volatility is a structurally different construction from the archive's numerator-adjustment attempts and is dimensionally coherent, though the three-annual-observation volatility estimate is noisy and the signal risks being dominated by B/M with the accrual-quality term contributing little variation.

This is the archived "EBITDA Accrual Rank Gap Trap" multiplied by a positive accrual-persistence rank, so it is a cosmetic re-weighting of an already-tested expression whose signed base term makes the multiplicative interaction sign-unstable (for negative gaps, higher persistence pushes the signal in the opposite direction from the stated hypothesis) and whose predictive content may be entirely the standalone accrual anomaly leg.

critic_notes.target_name: Operating Working Capital Clean Sales Yield
critic_notes.rationale: It is the same one-sided-cap yield template already tested four times in the archive (earnings, EBITDA, cash-flow, cash-flow-statement sales) with the numerator base swapped, and because sales are typically an order of magnitude larger than one-year working-capital accruals the cap almost never binds materially, so the signal collapses to the well-known sales-to-price anomaly.

Direct rediscovery of the archive's rank-gap template ("Reported Clean Earnings Rank Gap", "EBITDA Accrual Rank Gap Trap") with book equity substituted, and since ceq dwarfs one-year accruals for most firms the haircut rarely changes the rank, leaving a mostly-zero signal driven by a small tail of low-book-equity firms.

critic_notes.target_name: Accrual Noise Discounted Cash Flow Yield
critic_notes.rationale: The absolute-accrual (earnings-quality) angle is a mild conceptual advance over the archive's volatility/deterioration surcharges, but it reuses the same denominator-surcharge template, the surcharge is small relative to market cap so the signal largely reproduces the known cash-flow-to-price effect, and for negative-oancf firms the surcharge perversely improves the score.

critic_notes.target_name: Own History Accrual Spike Earnings Trap
critic_notes.rationale: The surcharge at*TS_RANK can reach a full multiple of assets, so the rank gap is dominated by asset-to-market rather than accrual timing — meaning high values mostly identify high book-to-market value firms, whose positive expected returns contradict the stated negative sign — and the gap also inverts for loss-making firms.

This is the only proposal introducing genuinely new economic content relative to the archive's working-capital accrual theme (depreciation-conservatism conditioning of B/M), the one-sided surcharge is internally consistent with the positive expected sign, though the penalty magnitude is small enough relative to market cap that the signal risks being little more than book-to-market.

The MIN is bounded above by E/P, so high values are substantially driven by cheapness (a positive predictor), contradicting the stated negative expected sign, and the "cheap-on-reported-earnings-but-accrual-funded" trap channel was already tested as the Reported Clean Earnings Rank Gap.

MIN(E/P, −accruals/P) is a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived One Sided Accrual Capped Earnings Yield (MIN(ib, ib−accruals)/P), differing only in whether the earnings level is retained in the second leg, so it is unlikely to deliver substantively new evidence.

Book-to-price is typically an order of magnitude larger than accruals-to-price, so the MIN will almost always select the accrual leg and the signal degenerates into a plain price-scaled Sloan accrual measure rather than the intended value×accrual interaction.

This is the isolated trap leg of the already-evaluated Underdepreciation Discounted Book Yield with no value interaction, is close to the known Lev–Thiagarajan/Abarbanell–Bushee depreciation-change fundamental signal, and the one-sided MAX leaves a large mass of exact zeros that will make one portfolio leg unstable.

Adding back only the firm-relative abnormal excess depreciation to earnings is a coherent, sign-consistent value×conservative-accounting construct that is a genuine complement (not a mirror) to the archived underdepreciation-discount signal and uses a distinct accrual channel from the working-capital family that dominates the archive.

EBITDA/EV is typically much larger than WC-accruals/EV so the MIN mostly returns the accrual term, collapsing to an EV-scaled accrual anomaly, and the intended trap channel duplicates the archived EBITDA Accrual Rank Gap Trap with the same negative sign.

This is essentially the archive's "Reported Earnings Accrual Reliance Trap" with a one-year difference applied to the reliance ratio, a cosmetic level-to-change variant whose DELTA of a ratio with a volatile, sign-unstable |ib|+|oancf| denominator adds mostly noise rather than new economics.

critic_notes.target_name: Book Value Clean Earnings Deficit Trap
critic_notes.rationale: The construction is internally consistent (cheap book equity plus negative three-year clean earnings yields high scores, matching the negative expected sign) and meaningfully differs from the archive's denominator-penalty version by targeting the short side, though much of the predictive content may come from the standalone cumulative-profitability leg rather than the interaction.

This recombines two already-tested archive components — the EV-floored EBITDA yield and the |ebitda|-scaled working-capital reliance share of "Working Capital Share Adjusted EBITDA Yield" — into a multiplicative trap, making it an incremental re-parameterization of a tested idea rather than a substantively new mechanism.

The recch sign convention is handled correctly and the cheap-revenue-with-uncollected-sales trap is coherently specified, but the receivable-accrual leg is close to a known Sloan-style earnings-quality anomaly and recch's ~8% coverage in this archive limits how much new evidence it can generate.

This is structurally the same expression as the receivable proposal with sale substituted for the near-identical revt and invch for recch, so it is a within-batch near-duplicate whose accrual leg largely rediscovers the published inventory-growth anomaly.

The signed depreciation shortfall relative to the firm's own recent policy is the least crowded content in this archive and the trap construction is directionally consistent, though it reuses the same rank-times-reliance template and overlaps in spirit with the already-tested "Depreciation Normalized Earnings Yield".

This is the book-equity analogue of the already-tested "Conservative Depreciation Earnings Yield," and because one year of abnormal depreciation is minuscule relative to ceq, the signal will be nearly indistinguishable from plain book-to-market — a cosmetic variant that mostly rediscovers value.

This is a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived "Underdepreciation Earnings Reliance Trap" (MA replaced by TS_MAX), and because TS_MAX minus current is always non-negative, the interaction loses the abnormality interpretation and instead loads on the level/volatility of depreciation intensity.

The sign logic is internally inconsistent: a positive txach means tax expense charged against ib exceeds cash taxes paid, which makes reported *earnings* conservative (it boosts oancf, not ib), so pairing it with an earnings-yield rank and a negative expected sign contradicts the stated mechanism.

This is a direct base-yield swap of the already-tested "Opaque Other Accrual Earnings Trap" (ib → ceq), which the archive shows to be a weak channel, and it adds no new economic content beyond the substitution.

It is essentially the sign-flipped mirror of the archived "Receivable Reliance Revenue Trap," and its economics directly contradict the sibling "Inventory Liquidation Cash Yield Trap" logic (working-capital release treated as good here, unsustainable there) without resolving which interpretation holds.

The expression matches the hypothesis and sign (apalch positive = payables-funded cash inflow, interacted with cheap-on-cash-flow rank, expected negative), and it is a substantively motivated short-side reformulation of the previously failed long-side payables adjustments, though it remains close to prior work on the same channel.

This is essentially the archived "Depreciation Conservatism Book Interaction" with RANK(B/M) swapped for SUMRANK(B/M, E/P), a cosmetic re-weighting of the value leg whose stated motivation (reducing value-factor exposure) is backwards since adding earnings yield increases, not reduces, HML loading.

A defensible, mechanism-driven refinement of the archive's strongest result — industry-adjusting the own-history depreciation surprise removes sector-common accounting/asset-mix variation and is a genuinely different conditioning construct rather than a rescaling, though it remains a close relative of that prior signal.

Near-duplicate of the archived "Underdepreciation Earnings Reliance Trap" (same scaled depreciation-shortfall conditioner, same sign, same construction) with only the value leg widened to SUMRANK, so it adds little new information beyond the already-evaluated short side.

A coherent and previously untested conditioner (D&A addback dependence of OCF as unpriced capital consumption) that complements rather than duplicates the archive's working-capital and maintenance-depreciation work, though dpc/(|oancf|+|ib|) is largely a capital-intensity/industry proxy so any result will need an industry-neutral robustness check.

The sign logic is internally consistent and the txach interpretation is correct, but this is substantially a sign-flipped repackaging of the archived "Tax Deferred Cash Yield Trap" (same conditioner, same scaler, adjacent value leg) whose positive fmb slope came with negligible alpha and ~6% coverage, so the "new" evidence is likely the same underlying result relabeled.

The acceleration framing is a legitimately distinct construct from the archive's level and one-period-change accrual conditioners, but taking a second difference of a ratio whose numerator is already an annual first difference stacks three layers of annual noise and will require several extra years of history, so expect weak power and degraded coverage.

This is the third variant of the same archived signal (raw and IND_ADJ versions already tested, with IND_ADJ marginally weakening the portfolio alpha), so swapping in IND_ZSCORE is a cosmetic normalization change rather than a new mechanism.

Internally consistent and the industry-capital-intensity concern is legitimate, but it is a single-operator overlay on the already-evaluated "Underdepreciation Earnings Reliance Trap," and the archive's own evidence shows IND_ADJ did not improve the analogous book-value case.

Since oancf already adds depreciation back, subtracting a smoothed dp charge collapses the measure to roughly a cash-earnings-to-price ratio, making this a near-rediscovery of standard earnings/cash-flow yield rather than a cross-theme interaction, and it closely echoes the archived Maintenance Depreciation EBITDA Yield.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry Adjusted Depreciation Burden EBITDA Trap
critic_notes.rationale: Beyond being an IND_ADJ overlay on the archived Depreciation Burdened EBITDA Trap, the economic content reduces to the well-documented point that EBIT/EV dominates EBITDA/EV for capital-consuming firms.

This changes the conditioning variable substantively (persistent depreciation-intensity elevation versus a one-year surprise) rather than merely renormalizing an existing signal, and the sign logic matches the archive's strongest channel, though the MA3-versus-MA5 windows overlap heavily and may deliver little independent information.

Mechanically consistent but it is an IND_ADJ overlay on the already-evaluated Reported Earnings Accrual Reliance Trap, and the underlying content is essentially the Sloan accrual anomaly crossed with E/P.

The depreciation-surprise leg is byte-identical to the archive's strongest signal (Depreciation Conservatism Book Interaction) and only the value leg is swapped from book/market to book-EV/EV — a third cosmetic variant of the same family after the book and asset-yield versions, with no diagnosis of why the leverage/cash adjustment should matter.

This is essentially the sign-mirrored, unscaled twin of the archived "Underdepreciation Earnings Reliance Trap" (same earnings-yield rank leg, same dp/at vs MA(dp/at,3) surprise), and the hypothesis wording is muddled since the value leg uses reported ib, which is mechanically depressed by the very depreciation elevation being rewarded.

Netting the depreciation-surprise leg against asset-scaled working-capital accruals is a genuinely new composite that tests whether the accrual channel adds incrementally to the archive's best depreciation result, though there is a real risk the known-strong depreciation leg simply dominates a noisy accrual term that has repeatedly failed in this archive.

Internally inconsistent mechanism — operating cash flow adds depreciation back and is essentially invariant to depreciation policy, so "cheap cash flow supported by understated asset consumption" does not follow; it is also just the archived Underdepreciation Earnings Reliance Trap with oancf substituted for ib in the value leg.

Another value-leg swap onto the already-tested depreciation-conservatism interaction, with a weaker link (dividends are a cash payout only loosely tied to depreciation policy) and likely reduced, dividend-payer-only coverage that risks overstating improvement.
